newsitem.title: FRANCE: Interview-Chateauroux expansion banks on general cargo traffic.
newsitem.headline: Interview-Chateauroux expansion banks on general cargo traffic.

text.p: Chateauroux-Deols airport in central France said it is banking on a strong growth in its general cargo traffic in 1997.

"In 1996, general cargo represented several hundreds of tonnes of traffic and our aim for the current year is to swell this to several thousands of tonnes," the airport's general manager, Martin Fraissignes, told Reuters.
1996 global air cargo throughput at Chateauroux airport, formerly a military airfield, totalled 1,245 tonnes, up 54.5 percent on 1995, figures issued by France's airports authority federation show.

"In the first quarter of 1997, for the first time ever, general cargo surpassed military cargo in terms of tonnage. , In the first week of March alone, we handled as much general cargo as in the first two months of the year and during the whole of 1996," Fraissignes said.
"Our mid-term objective, covering the next two to three years is to increase global annual throughput to 25,000 tonnes," he added.
General cargo, carried to and from Chateauroux on charter flights, was largely made up of cigarettes, automobiles, automotive parts and perishables.

The southern republics of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) was the main destination for cigarettes while other charter routes link Chateauroux with West Africa, the Middle East, Egypt and Jordan, being two examples and the Far East, including Thailand and Indonesia, Fraissignes added.

"We are targeting the development of perishables traffic from West Africa -- especially green beans, pineapples and mangoes -- and through the exploitation of our geographical position we are set on capturing shipments which now transit via Ostend airport and are destined for Paris and northern France," he said.
Proximity to the A71 motorway puts Chateauroux airport within two-and-a-half hours of Paris by truck and especially for perishables traffic, the Rungis wholesale market near Orly airport.

"We see ourselves emerging as one of five "industrial" airports in the European Union -- the others being Stansted, Ostend, Hahn in Germany and Vittoria in Spain -- used by shippers for full-freighter flights and viewed as an alternative to the major, national gateways where traffic congestion is often a problem."
France's junior transport minister, Anne-Marie Idrac visited Chateauroux airport last month to lend her support to the development of the site.

"Chateauroux is cutting a niche for itself as an all-cargo airport and the French government is totally behind it and will give all the authorisations necessary to encourage airlines to locate at the airport," Idrac said.
The main cargo charter operator at Chateauroux is French company, Efis Cargo, which has a Lockheed Hercules L382G freighter based at the airport.
The aircraft is being leased from the South African company, Safair Ltd.
"Since Efis began charter flights with the Hercules in July 1996, it has been flying around 100 hours a month," an Efis official told Reuters.

The most frequent routes operated by the L382G freighter are South America -- Brazil and Argentina -- and the Gulf States -- Qatar and Oman -- with military cargos the most common shipments, the official added.
Efis has also chartered Antonov 124 flights from Chateauroux.
"We are in negotiations with other charter operators and are hopeful of a positive outcome between now and end-June," , Fraissignes said.
He added that next month, adding he would visit the U.S. and Latin America on a marketing mission next month with Miami, Colombia and Chile as key destinations.

"Miami is the hub for air cargo to and from Latin America while in Colombia there is scope to develop an export trade to Chateauroux in fresh flowers on a round-the-year basis and from Chile with winter season shipments of red fruits.
